data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy": null, "claim": "Preferring the better-corroborated theory is defensible on Popper's terms as a non-inductive, critical selection rule based on 'verisimilitude' (truth-likeness) and informational content, but accepting this defense costs the admission that science cannot offer rational assurance of future success, only a rationale for preferring the most severely tested (and thus most falsifiable) conjectures as the best current approximations to truth.", "counterconditions": [{"case": "If the Tichý/Miller proof holds that verisimilitude cannot be formally defined or compared between false theories, then the claim that corroboration tracks truth-likeness collapses.", "checker_spec": null, "eval": "observation"}, {"case": "If 'acting on a theory' logically entails an expectation of its future reliability (a probabilistic stance), then the preference smuggles in induction regardless of Popper's semantic distinctions.", "checker_spec": null, "eval": "observation"}, {"case": "If the distinction between 'informational content' and 'predictive power' is untenable when practical stakes (like building bridges) are involved, the non-inductive defense fails.", "checker_spec": null, "eval": "observation"}], "definitions": [], "derivation": [], "formalization_refs": [], "mechanism": "The mechanism distinguishes between 'justification' (which implies induction) and 'critical preference.' Popper argues we prefer theories with higher empirical content because they are more informative and have survived stricter tests. This preference is not a prediction that the theory will remain true (induction), but a strategic choice to act on the theory that has withstood the most severe attempts at refutation, thereby maximizing our proximity to truth (verisimilitude) without claiming probability. The 'cost' is the abandonment of the desire for certainty or probabilistic security in action; we act on the best guess, acknowledging it may fail tomorrow.", "premises": [], "schema": "deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1", "scope": {"covers": [], "excludes": []}, "simulation_refs": [], "uncertainties": []}
